page: Microsoft Azure D4ds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon 8573C cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz and includes a 260 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 236 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance supports Premium Storage. No GPU accelerators are included.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2165.0 and single-threaded Gzip compression reaching 31.43 GB/sec. However, multi-core performance is more modest, as reflected in a weak stress-ng multi-core score of 3984.38 and a weak multi-threaded Bzip3 decompression rate. Memory bandwidth is a notable bottleneck, scoring in the bottom 25% for both cached small-block and uncached large-block read/write operations. Conversely, text processing and basic database operations perform in the average to strong range.

Given its hardware profile and benchmark characteristics, the D4ds_v6 is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that demand high single-core CPU speeds but do not saturate memory bandwidth. It is well-suited for general-purpose applications, static web serving, text processing, and lightweight database operations. It is less optimal for memory-bandwidth-intensive tasks, heavy multi-threaded software compilation, or ray tracing.
